Hu et al. (2020) Thermal Runaway Model

Overview

LiionTR includes a reduced-order thermal runaway reaction network based on the model reported by Hu et al. (2020).

The model represents thermal runaway using four principal reaction states:

  1. SEI decomposition;

  2. anode-electrolyte reaction;

  3. cathode decomposition;

  4. electrolyte decomposition.

Each reaction contributes heat according to its kinetic rate, reaction progress state, reacting-material content, and reaction enthalpy.

The model is implemented in

liiontr.library.hu2020.

Reference

The thermal runaway model implemented in LiionTR is based on the work of Hu et al. [Hu et al., 2020].

The original study developed a numerical lithium-ion battery thermal runaway model incorporating multiple internal side reactions, including SEI, anode, cathode, and electrolyte reactions.

LiionTR converts the reported model parameters to SI units before constructing the reaction network.

Reaction Network

The reaction-state vector is

\[\boldsymbol{\alpha} = \left[ \alpha_{\mathrm{SEI}}, \alpha_{\mathrm{anode}}, \alpha_{\mathrm{cathode}}, \alpha_{\mathrm{electrolyte}} \right].\]

The corresponding progress equations have the generic form

\[\frac{d\alpha_i}{dt} = k_i(T) f_i(\boldsymbol{\alpha}).\]

The total heat-generation rate is obtained by summing the contributions of all reactions.

Initial Reaction State

LiionTR initializes the Hu et al. reaction network using

\[\boldsymbol{\alpha}_0 = \left[ 0.85, 0.25, 0.04, 0.00 \right].\]

These values correspond respectively to:

SEI Decomposition

The SEI decomposition reaction uses Arrhenius kinetics,

\[k_{\mathrm{SEI}}(T) = A_{\mathrm{SEI}} \exp\left( -\frac{ E_{a,\mathrm{SEI}} }{ R T } \right).\]

SEI Unit Conversion

The reported reaction enthalpy is converted as

\[257 \ \mathrm{J/g} = 257000 \ \mathrm{J/kg}.\]

The reported volumetric reactant content is converted as

\[6.104\times10^{5} \ \mathrm{g/m^3} = 610.4 \ \mathrm{kg/m^3}.\]

The original initial remaining fraction is 0.15.

Because LiionTR uses reaction conversion,

\[\alpha = 1-r,\]

the initial SEI conversion is

\[\alpha_{\mathrm{SEI},0} = 1-0.15 = 0.85.\]

Anode Unit Conversion

The reaction enthalpy conversion is

\[1714 \ \mathrm{J/g} = 1.714\times10^{6} \ \mathrm{J/kg}.\]

The initial remaining fraction is 0.75, giving

\[\alpha_{\mathrm{anode},0} = 1-0.75 = 0.25.\]

SEI-Dependent Anode Activation

The anode-electrolyte reaction is coupled to the state of the SEI reaction.

In the current LiionTR implementation, the reaction becomes active only after the remaining SEI fraction falls below a prescribed threshold.

The remaining SEI fraction is

\[r_{\mathrm{SEI}} = 1-\alpha_{\mathrm{SEI}}.\]

The threshold is

\[r_{\mathrm{SEI}} < 0.10.\]

This introduces a coupling between the SEI and anode-electrolyte reaction states.

Exponential Inhibition

The anode reaction also includes an exponential inhibition term.

Conceptually,

\[f_{\mathrm{anode}} = f_{\mathrm{base}} \exp(-x_{\mathrm{SEI}}),\]

where \(x_{\mathrm{SEI}}\) is obtained from the normalized remaining SEI state.

This captures the effect of the remaining SEI layer on the anode-electrolyte reaction.

Cathode Decomposition

The cathode decomposition is represented using two parallel kinetic channels that share a single cathode conversion.

The reaction is active only above

\[T_{\mathrm{cathode}} = 393.15 \ \mathrm{K}.\]

Cathode Reactant Content

The reported cathode content is

\[1.221\times10^{6} \ \mathrm{g/m^3}.\]

LiionTR converts this to

\[1221 \ \mathrm{kg/m^3}.\]

Shared Cathode Progress

Both cathode channels share the same reaction conversion,

\[\alpha_{\mathrm{cathode}}.\]

The implemented progress law is autocatalytic,

\[f_{\mathrm{cathode}} = \alpha_{\mathrm{cathode}} \left( 1-\alpha_{\mathrm{cathode}} \right).\]

The initial cathode conversion is

\[\alpha_{\mathrm{cathode},0} = 0.04.\]

Cathode Heat Generation

Because both channels share one reaction state, their heat-generation contributions are summed.

Conceptually,

\[\dot{q}_{\mathrm{cathode}} = w_{\mathrm{cathode}} f_{\mathrm{cathode}} \left[ \Delta H_1 k_1(T) + \Delta H_2 k_2(T) \right].\]

This structure is represented using a LiionTR multi-channel reaction.

Electrolyte Decomposition

Electrolyte decomposition is modeled using Arrhenius kinetics and a temperature threshold.

The implemented threshold is

\[T_{\mathrm{electrolyte}} = 473.15 \ \mathrm{K}.\]

Reaction Ordering

LiionTR preserves the following ordering throughout the network:

0  SEI decomposition
1  Anode-electrolyte
2  Cathode decomposition
3  Electrolyte decomposition

The conversion vector therefore follows

\[\boldsymbol{\alpha} = [ \alpha_{\mathrm{SEI}}, \alpha_{\mathrm{anode}}, \alpha_{\mathrm{cathode}}, \alpha_{\mathrm{electrolyte}} ].\]

Cell-Mass Conversion

Several parameters in the literature model are specified as reactant content per unit cell volume.

LiionTR converts a volumetric reactant content \(W_i\) to a cell mass fraction using

\[w_i = \frac{W_i}{\rho_{\mathrm{cell}}},\]

where \(\rho_{\mathrm{cell}}\) is the effective cell density.

The reaction heat-generation rate then becomes

\[\dot{Q}_i = m_{\mathrm{cell}} w_i \Delta H_i \dot{\alpha}_i.\]

Coupling to the Thermal Model

The total heat-generation rate is

\[\dot{Q}_{\mathrm{gen}} = \sum_i \dot{Q}_i.\]

This value is supplied to the lumped thermal model,

\[C_{\mathrm{th}} \frac{dT}{dt} = \dot{Q}_{\mathrm{gen}} - h A \left( T-T_{\infty} \right).\]

The resulting increase in temperature accelerates the Arrhenius kinetics and produces the thermal-runaway feedback loop.

Current LiionTR Representation

The Hu et al. model is represented using the generic LiionTR architecture rather than a single monolithic model class.

The mapping is approximately:

Hu model
   |
   +-- SEI
   |     +-- Arrhenius
   |     +-- volumetric reaction parameters
   |
   +-- Anode-electrolyte
   |     +-- Arrhenius
   |     +-- SEI-dependent threshold
   |     +-- exponential inhibition
   |
   +-- Cathode
   |     +-- channel 1 Arrhenius
   |     +-- channel 2 Arrhenius
   |     +-- temperature threshold
   |     +-- shared autocatalytic conversion
   |
   +-- Electrolyte
         +-- Arrhenius
         +-- temperature threshold

             |
             v

       ReactionNetwork

Implementation

The complete reaction network is constructed by

liiontr.library.hu2020.hu2020_reaction_network().

The initial conversion vector is provided by

liiontr.library.hu2020.hu2020_initial_conversions().

SEI parameters are provided by

liiontr.library.hu2020.hu2020_sei_decomposition().

Anode-electrolyte parameters are provided by

liiontr.library.hu2020.hu2020_anode_electrolyte().

Its coupled progress model is constructed by

liiontr.library.hu2020.hu2020_anode_progress_model().

The cathode reaction is constructed by

liiontr.library.hu2020.hu2020_cathode_decomposition().

Electrolyte parameters are provided by

liiontr.library.hu2020.hu2020_electrolyte_decomposition().

The complete electrolyte reaction is constructed by

liiontr.library.hu2020.hu2020_electrolyte_reaction().

Scope and Limitations

The LiionTR implementation should be interpreted as a reduced-order representation of the Hu et al. thermal runaway model.

It currently focuses on:

  • reaction kinetics;

  • reaction progress;

  • heat generation;

  • coupling to a lumped thermal state.

Gas chemistry, chemical equilibrium, multiphase behavior, detailed electrochemistry, and internal spatial temperature gradients are not part of the Hu reaction-network implementation itself.

These processes may be coupled to the reaction model through other LiionTR subsystems as the framework evolves.
